The Rangers have challenged him with aggressive assignments, and he has fared well while reaching High-A at age 17 and Double-A at 18. The youngest batting qualifier (age 19) at Double-A last season, he ranked as the top prospect in the Texas League while batting .255/.355/.386 with career bests in walk (13 percent) and strikeout (20 percent) rate. He played just one game in the Arizona Fall League afterward because of arm fatigue, then was diagnosed with a torn elbow ligament in February that required internal brace surgery that will cost him the first half of the 2026 season.

afl-player/808234.bonusEvidence: Quintero trained as a catcher in Venezuela, but the Dodgers made him a full-time center fielder after signing him for $297,500 because they wanted to make the most of his athleticism and offensive potential. He dominated Rookie-level pitching while winning championships in the Dominican Summer and Arizona Complex leagues in his first two years as a pro, then earned California League MVP and Prospect of the Year accolades at age 19 in 2025. He slashed .306/.426/.533 with 14 homers and 35 steals in 81 games, leading the Single-A circuit in on-base percentage, slugging, OPS (.959) and longballs and placing third in batting before spending the final six weeks in High-A.

dsl-player/829769.summary: Signed by the New York Yankees on December 1, 2025.
dsl-player/829769.bonusEvidence: Scouting grades: Hit: 40 | Power: 55 | Run: 55 | Arm: 65 | Field: 50 | Overall: 40 Pena originally agreed to sign with the Cardinals for $300,000 in January 2025 before the deal got scuttled, then inked with the Yankees for $357,533 that November. Assigned to Single-A afterward, he impressed by slashing .323/.389/.552 with six homers and 10 steals in 24 games.

dsl-player/836353.name: Francisco Renteria
dsl-player/836353.summary: Signed by the Philadelphia Phillies on January 15, 2026.
dsl-player/836353.bonusEvidence: Renteria came in at No. 3 on MLB Pipeline’s Top 50 International Prospects list when the 2026 signing period opened in January. His combination of experience in travel ball, on the international scene at events like the 15U World Cup and his success at age 15 in the Venezuelan Major League last summer made him a hot commodity. The Phillies jumped in to get the talented outfielder who trained with César Suárez at CJ Baseball Academy, a member of MLB’s Trainer Partnership Program, for $4 million and executives in the organization are having a hard time containing their excitement.

dsl-player/835022.name: Ricki Moneys
dsl-player/835022.summary: Signed by the Milwaukee Brewers on January 15, 2026.
dsl-player/835022.bonusEvidence: The Brewers’ success in scouting and developing international talent has become a well-documented story across the industry, and it was certainly notable when the organization signed three of MLB Pipeline’s Top 50 international prospects at the opening of the 2026 window in January. At No. 20, Moneys was the highest-ranked of the three, ahead of No. 24 Diego Frontado and No. 49 José Rodríguez, but signed the third-highest bonus of the group at $1.15 million. The Dominican Republic native has opened his Minor League career in the Dominican Summer League, where he’s met much of the pre-signing hype.

dsl-player/837522.summary: Signed by the Houston Astros on January 15, 2026.

He received the highest bonus in Houston's crop this year, signing for $2,147,500. Besides his tools, scouts also like his makeup and how he plays the game with swagger.

dsl-player/836584.summary: Signed by the Athletics on January 15, 2026.
dsl-player/836584.bonusEvidence: The No. 5 prospect during the 2026 international signing period, Colome signed with the A’s out of the Dominican Republic for $4 million. He’s the latest member of the Colome family legacy joining the professional baseball ranks, following the footsteps of his father, Jesus Colome, who spent 10 big league seasons as a reliever with four different clubs from 2001-10. Johenssy is also the cousin of former MLB reliever Alex Colome. On his mother’s side, two of his uncles were top Minor League prospects, providing plenty of family support as he prepares for the journey of playing baseball at the highest of levels.

dsl-player/836592.summary: Signed by the San Diego Padres on January 15, 2026.
dsl-player/836592.bonusEvidence: The Padres typically have been heavy hitters on the international market, targeting the very best players, but spread money around more than usual in their 2026 class. Their top signing was Cuban shortstop Hernandez, who trained in the Dominican Republic before turning pro for $1.4 million in January. He played well in the Rookie-level Dominican Summer League before San Diego traded him and right-hander Miguel Mendez to obtain Robbie Ray from the Giants at the Trade Deadline in August.

Milwaukee went back to the South American country for its biggest international signing in 2026, bringing in Frontado (MLB Pipeline’s No. 24 prospect in the class) for $1.6 million in January.

dsl-player/836583.summary: Signed by the New York Mets on January 15, 2026.

After being considered arguably the most advanced offensive player in this year’s international group, he signed with the Mets for $3.9 million at the opening of the window on Jan. 15.

It was the third-largest sum the Rays have given an international amateur, trailing only the bonuses given to Wander Franco ($3.85 million) and Brailer Guerrero ($3.7 million). It’s a big bet on a young player with a long way to go and extraordinary upside.

Ranked as the No. 22 international prospect in the 2026 class by MLB Pipeline, Suárez signed with the Royals for $1,647,500 this past winter; only Angeibel Gomez ($2,797,500) signed for more with Kansas City this cycle.

dsl-player/834311.summary: Signed by the Pittsburgh Pirates on January 15, 2026.

But it's been Tejera, a much more under-the-radar signing at $90,000, who has jumped to the forefront during the class's pro debut. While the Dominican outfielder's surface numbers in the Dominican Summer League didn't jump off the page, the metrics underneath those were so impressive the Pirates pushed him stateside to the Florida Complex League after just 18 DSL games.
